---
title: "Report 5 · Causal attribution of crime"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("../R/report_setup.R")
all_items <- paste0("attribution_", 1:9)
```

The nine items (Carroll et al., 1987) contain two kinds of explanation for crime: **circumstances** (family problems, poverty, flaws in society, situations) and **the person** (laziness, deliberate choice, disregard for others). They are reported as **two separate scores**; the reasons are in the last section.

# Societal attribution

```{r}
#| include: false
score      <- "attr_societal"
item_names <- paste0("attribution_", c(1, 4, 5, 6))
subscales  <- list()
lo <- 1; hi <- 7
```

{{< include _construct_template.qmd >}}

# Individual attribution

```{r}
#| include: false
score      <- "attr_individual"
item_names <- paste0("attribution_", 7:9)
```

{{< include _construct_template.qmd >}}

# Why two scores

**Direction check.** Across the nine items there are 9-12 negative inter-item correlations in every wave, so one average of all nine would mix opposite explanations.

**Structure.** An exploratory factor analysis in wave 1 gave two factors that are almost uncorrelated, so respondents can endorse both kinds of explanation at once. Items 2 (drugs) and 3 (learning from criminals) were left out because they load on both factors or fit neither clearly. The structure was found in wave 1 and is checked in waves 2-5 here:

```{r}
fits <- NULL
for (w in 1:5) fits <- rbind(fits, cbind(Wave = w, efa(d[d$wave == w, ], all_items, 2)$fit))
show_table(fits, digits = 3)
```

**Loadings in wave 1** (two factors; below .30 hidden):

```{r}
show_table(efa(d[d$wave == 1, ], all_items, 2)$loadings)
```

**Loadings in wave 5:**

```{r}
show_table(efa(d[d$wave == 5, ], all_items, 2)$loadings)
```

**Correlation between the two scores:**

```{r}
cors <- NULL
for (w in 1:5) {
  dw <- d[d$wave == w, ]
  cors <- rbind(cors, correlation(dw$attr_societal, dw$attr_individual, paste("Wave", w)))
}
show_table(cors)
```
